items.author: Kellie Lunney
items.title: Senate Permitting Legislation Advances, Setting up Final Push
items.summary: Lunney reports the Senate voted 65-31 to close debate on the bill, approved another managers' amendment 69-27, and expects a final passage vote early Friday.

quote.text: Lawmakers voted 65-31 to bring to a close debate on the bill, which would speed up permitting reviews for energy and infrastructure projects.
quote.speaker: Kellie Lunney, Bloomberg Law

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: The Surprising Senate Votes in the Bipartisan Permitting Bill
items.summary: Meyer tallies who has stayed with or left the bill across the cloture votes, noting Hawley and several Democrats voted no on the Nov. 18 cloture vote.

quote.text: Mike Rounds, the junior senator from South Dakota, is the only Republican to vote no in every roll call.
quote.speaker: Robinson Meyer, Heatmap

items.title: Wednesday, November 18, 2026
items.summary: The Senate's floor log records the 70-26 waiver of the Merkley budget point of order, 69-27 adoption of the Capito substitute #6883, and 65-31 cloture on H.R. 2347.

quote.text: By a vote of 70-26, the Senate agreed to the motion to waive the Budget Act with respect to the Merkley budget point-of-order in relation to Capito substitute amendment #6883 to H.R. 2347, the legislative vehicle for permitting reform.
quote.speaker: U.S. Senate Daily Press

items.author: Sarah Liese
items.title: Senate expected to vote on permitting bill tribal leaders in Oklahoma, beyond oppose
items.summary: Liese reports tribal leaders including Muscogee Nation Principal Chief David Hill and NCAI President Mark Macarro oppose the bill's Section 106 changes ahead of the final vote.

quote.text: Any amendment to S. 5653 merely puts lipstick on a pig
quote.speaker: Mark Macarro, NCAI President, as quoted by KGOU

items.author: Orion Donovan Smith
items.title: Cantwell, Murray and Northwest tribal leaders oppose bipartisan permitting reform bill as it nears Senate passage
items.summary: Donovan Smith reports Sen. Cantwell and Northwest tribal leaders made a last appeal against the bill's Section 106 changes, with Murray, Wyden and Merkley also opposed.

quote.text: But this bill, as it’s currently drafted, is not the answer.
quote.speaker: Sen. Maria Cantwell, as quoted by The Spokesman-Review

items.author: Stephen Prager
items.title: Schumer Faces Fresh Call to Step Aside Over Latest Vote With GOP on Polluter-Friendly Permitting Bill
items.summary: Prager reports Food & Water Watch's Jim Walsh called for Sen. Schumer to step down as Democratic leader after he was among 14 Democrats voting for cloture 65-31.

quote.text: Sen. Schumer’s alignment with Republicans over a majority of his own Democratic caucus in voting to advance this terrible pro-polluter, pro-data center permitting bill is all the reason needed to demand that Schumer step down as leader of the Senate Democrats.
quote.speaker: Jim Walsh, policy director, Food & Water Watch, as quoted by Common Dreams
